 ‘Terrible joke’ that cost A-lister the role of James Bond 
 Mikala Theocharous November 21, 2026 - 12.05am 
 shares Share article Matthew Rhys lost the role of 007 to Daniel Craig after telling a “terrible joke” during the audition process.
 Rhys confessed the blunder came after producers asked him what he would “do differently” if he got the chance to play the iconic character in a resurfaced interview with Conan O’Brien from 2023.
 Matthew Rhys lost the role of 007 to Daniel Craig after making a “terrible” joke.   Youtube 
 Advertisement “Is this a trick question, or is it a genuine question?” Rhys recalled thinking to himself before making “a terrible joke” that Bond should walk with a limp. 
 “It got worse. It went very quiet,” he recalled. “So I thought I would double down, and said, ‘Eye patch.’ And then I just fell apart. And it lasted about 30 seconds after that.”
 The Widow’s Bay star confessed he “still doesn’t have a coherent answer that would’ve wowed” the producers and said he “often wonders” how Craig responded. 
 Craig played the iconic character across five films, with his tenure ending in 2021 with No Time To Die .

 Rhys added that he was so confident that he was gonna get the role that he “told so many people” he had gotten the gig.
 “I practically told my family I was going to be [Bond],” he said. 
 Rhys is part of a long list of actors who were up for the iconic role but didn’t grab it. 
 Advertisement Superman actor   Henry Cavill, German-Irish actor Michael Fassbender, Outlander star Sam Heughan have all been up for the gig at one point. 
 Alex O’Loughlin, James Purefoy, Antony Starr and Julian McMahon have all also confirmed they were once in the running to play the Bond role that went to Craig.
 Daniel Craig would later be cast as James Bond.  FilmMagic 
 Of course, Robert Pattinson has been named the new Bond for Denis Villeneuve’s 007 film.

 A whole new list actors had reportedly participated in screen tests for the upcoming film. 
 The shortlist included Pattinson, Nicholas Hoult, Josh O’Connor, Callum Turner and Jack Lowden. 
 In a November 2026 interview with GQ Magazine after being named GQ’s Director of the Year, Villeneuve was asked about his upcoming Bond film.
 Advertisement Pattinson was a late frontrunner for the most recent Bond.  Jaap Buitendijk/Amazon MGM Studios via AP 
 While he was not able to share any concrete information about the film, the 59-year-old director shared that he has “the target of the sniper” on his chest.
 The director discussed how he is feeling the responsibility not to fail, adding, “We cannot f--- it up. We do not have the choice.”
 Villeneuve was directly asked if the role of James Bond has been cast yet, to which he replied, “It’s s--- in the process. In the process.”
 Advertisement Advertisement After the news was announced, Pattinson released a statement saying it was “the honour of a lifetime” to play the iconic role. 
 “James Bond is one of the most legendary characters in cinema, and to be entrusted with 007 is the honour of a lifetime,” the actor told Variety after news broke Monday, US time.
 Callum Turner, Josh O’Connor and Jack Lowden were in the running for the latest 007.   Nine/getty 
 “I’m deeply grateful to Denis, Amy, David, Tanya and everyone at Amazon MGM Studios for their belief in me,” he continued.
 Advertisement “To say this role is a dream come true is an understatement.
 “I couldn’t be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team.”
 The legendary character has previously been played by Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan and most recently, Craig.
